candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish the federal hospital requirement for restraint monitoring from locally specified monitoring intervals: the patient’s condition must be monitored at the interval set by hospital policy, subject to more restrictive applicable requirements.

options.A: Federal rules require the same once-per-shift reassessment interval for every restraint type and patient, so state law and facility policy cannot require closer monitoring.
options.B: Federal hospital rules require the restrained client’s condition to be monitored at an interval determined by hospital policy; additional state or facility requirements may be more restrictive or specific.
options.C: Once an order is written, nursing reassessment is unnecessary until the restraint causes an injury, the client requests removal, or the restraint order expires.
options.D: Every restraint requires the same 15-minute documentation interval until discharge because monitoring requirements do not vary with indication or clinical context.

candidate.rationale: Federal hospital regulation 42 CFR §482.13(e)(10) requires the condition of a restrained or secluded patient to be monitored by qualified staff at an interval determined by hospital policy. The same section also requires restraint or seclusion to end at the earliest possible time, and it separately imposes a one-hour face-to-face evaluation for restraint or seclusion used for violent or self-destructive behavior. Therefore, a universal once-per-shift, 15-minute, or other fixed federal interval does not apply to every nonviolent restraint.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For hospital restraint/seclusion, federal regulation requires monitoring at an interval determined by hospital policy; it does not establish a single fixed monitoring interval for every nonviolent restraint.
candidate.source_document_title: 42 CFR §482.13 — Condition of participation: Patient’s rights
candidate.source_locator: §482.13(e)(9)–(10) (earliest discontinuation; condition monitored at an interval determined by hospital policy) and §482.13(e)(12) (separate one-hour face-to-face rule for violent/self-destructive restraint or seclusion).

candidate.stem: A hospitalized client is placed in a restraint for a nonviolent safety indication after less-restrictive measures fail. The family asks, “Exactly how often must every hospital reassess this restraint?” Which response is most accurate?
